convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom indicator for Chaikin Volatility and custom Stochastic-like oscillator derived from it; intermediate derived values (HH, LL, raw stochastic) are computed manually in code rather than using a single built-in indicator, requiring replication of custom calculation logic in Python

derived_values.name: HH - Highest High of Chaikin Volatility over K period
LL - Lowest Low of Chaikin Volatility over K period

other_exits: Signal reversal can close opposite position when new entry signal occurs (close opposite then open new)

custom_logic_notes: The EA computes a Stochastic oscillator applied to Chaikin Volatility rather than price. The Chaikin Volatility is first obtained via iCustom call to a separate indicator file. Then HH/LL of the CV values are manually computed over KPeriod bars, and the raw stochastic, smoothed %K, and %D are calculated in the EA code. Digit adjustment is applied to SL/TP values: if _Digits is 5 or 3 (5-digit/3-digit broker), SL and TP input values are multiplied by 10. The IsNewBar guard ensures signals are evaluated once per completed bar using previous bar values ([1] vs [0]). Position gate ensures no duplicate positions - if an opposite signal occurs, the existing position is closed before opening the new one.
python_conversion_notes: 1) Must replicate Chaikin Volatility calculation in Python (HL spread SMA with rate-of-change) or use a library that provides it. 2) The Stochastic-of-CV is a two-step derived indicator requiring manual implementation: first compute CV series, then apply standard Stochastic formula to that series. 3) Digit adjustment logic must be preserved: detect 5/3-digit symbols and multiply SL/TP by 10 accordingly. 4) New-bar detection in Python requires tracking last seen bar timestamp. 5) Position management uses a 'close opposite then open new' pattern that must be preserved. 6) The iCustom call means the CV indicator source must be available or its algorithm reverse-engineered from the .mqh/custom indicator file.
